A fabric changes with the room around it — its scale, daylight, palette, texture, pattern and the amount of fabric the window requires. Find fabric for my room → Browse all fabrics ↓ LOOK CLOSERColour is only the beginning. SpaceLightColourWeightPatternTextureCharacter 01 / SPACEA little fabric.A much bigger presence.From a small detail to a wall of curtains: more fabric gives colour and pattern more presence. Lounge · the focal pointBedroom · the atmosphereBay · the architecturePatio doors · the expanse THE DETAIL → THE WHOLE ROOMLet the architecture set the scale.More fabric means more visual presence — even when the colours are quiet. What worksRead the curtains alongside the furniture and focal points.What needs careA strong repeat over a large area can become the room’s main event. 02 / LIGHTMeet the light.Then meet the fabric.One surface. Three light impressions. Check a sample in the light you actually live with. Bright daylightSee the colour relationship.Softer / lower lightNotice depth and quieter contrast.Warmer evening lightCheck how warmth changes the impression. One genuine fabric photograph, shown with illustrative light treatments — not measured colour rendering. Check your sample in your own daylight and evening light. A light-looking curtain can still have blackout lining.Face fabric shapes the look. Lining provides functional light control. 03 / COLOUROne room.More than one right answer.Start with the colours already in the picture. Then decide how you want the curtains to relate. PRIMARYWarm ivorySECONDARYBlue-greenACCENTDark timber An illustrative reading of this photograph, not a paint or colour-matching standard. BlendStay close to the foundation+A flax-like neutral follows the room’s warm ivory, keeping the overall relationship quiet. CoordinatePick up a supporting colour+A blue-green direction draws the curtain into conversation with the existing secondary colour. LiftIntroduce a lighter related tone+A soft chalk direction lightens the visual impression while staying related to the room. ContrastGive the curtain more presence+A deeper green creates stronger light–dark contrast. Across a large window, it will feel more assertive. 04 / WEIGHTWeight you can feel.Weight you can see.Physical weight is a supplier specification. Visual weight is the presence a fabric creates through colour, density, pattern and finish. Lighter presenceLight, view and softer boundaries.Balanced presenceA frame for the room and its furnishings.Stronger presenceDeeper colour brings the curtain forward. VISUAL WEIGHTWhat the room sees: colour depth, surface, pattern and the amount of fabric.PHYSICAL WEIGHTWhat the supplier specifies. Weave and construction also affect drape and movement; feel a sample before choosing. 05 / PATTERNNot just “patterned”.How much rhythm?Notice the space between motifs. The rhythm of the repeat. The strength of the contrast. A REPEATED DETAILAbeja · LinenClarke & Clarke A MORE EXPRESSIVE COMPOSITIONPainters Garden · Violet/CrimsonSanderson What worksConsider motif size, the space between motifs and the strength of the colour contrast together.What needs carePhotographs aren’t shown at a common physical scale. Check the repeat and see a sample before deciding. Prestigious Textiles · Cord · Breeze 06 / TEXTURE“Not plain.Not really patterned either.”Depth without a strong motif. Let the weave, surface and shifting shadows do the work.Look closerSee the surface here. Feel the handle with a sample. 07 / CHARACTERIt’s the combinationthat creates the character.No single colour or pattern defines a room. See what happens when the elements come together. CORD · BREEZE / PRESTIGIOUS TEXTILESLet the surface lead.A quieter rhythm. Interest in the weave. A GREEN & CREAM PATTERN STUDYLet the pattern lead.A more pronounced rhythm. Interest in the contrast. Related green directions, different visual activity. These are visual comparisons, not new product classifications. routes.text: .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 21px; padding-bottom: 21px; } @media screen and (min-width: 750px) { .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 28px; padding-bottom: 28px; } } FAQ Measuring & Ordering Q: How do I measure for curtains?A: Measure the full width of your window or pole including 10–15 cm overlap on each side. For drop, measure from the rod or track to 1 cm above the floor (or sill). See our detailed guide: How to Measure Curtains. Q: What fullness should I choose?A: Sheers & lightweight fabrics: 1.5× fabric width Standard drapes: 2× fabric width Luxury pinch/goblet pleats: 2.5–3× fabric width Heading Styles & Hardware Q: Which heading style works best with tracks?A: Wave (ripple fold) and pencil pleat headings glide smoothly on tracks. For rods, consider eyelet, tab‑top, or pinch pleat. Explore styles: Curtain Heading Styles. Q: Can I use my existing poles or tracks?A: In most cases, yes. Provide us with your current rod/track length and type during your consultation, and we’ll advise on compatibility or recommend hardware upgrades. Check our hardware range: Curtain Hardware & Tracks. Fabrics & Linings Q: Do I need blackout lining?A: Choose blackout lining for bedrooms, nurseries, or media rooms to block up to 99% of light and improve insulation. Standard lining offers UV protection and added weight. Learn more: Curtain Linings. Q: What fabrics are best for thermal efficiency?A: Thermal fleece linings or interlining behind heavy fabrics (velvet, chenille) trap heat. Thicker cotton or acrylic blends offer natural insulation for daytime use. Installation & Service Q: Do you offer professional installation?A: Yes—our certified fitters handle everything from accurate measuring to flawless hanging, including all hardware. Book now: Installation Service. Q: What’s the turnaround time?A: Custom curtains typically dispatch in 2–3 weeks. Installation appointments can be scheduled immediately upon delivery. Care & Maintenance Q: How do I wash my curtains?A: Machine‑washable fabrics: Gentle cycle, cold water, air‑dry. Heavier or interlined curtains: Dry clean only. Always check care labels and remove hooks or rings before cleaning. Q: How can I remove wrinkles?A: Use a handheld steamer on low heat. For wave or pencil pleats, steam from the back to maintain fold shape. Safety & Compliance Q: Are your curtains child‑safe?A: We offer cordless and tension‑rod systems to eliminate dangling cords, meeting the latest safety regulations for children’s rooms. . Q: Do you provide fire‑retardant fabrics?A: Yes—select fire‑retardant polyester options, ideal for commercial settings or nurseries. Contact us for certification details. Still Have Questions? If you don’t see your question here, get in touch with our design team or call us at 0800 772 067. We’re happy to help!

routes.text: .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 21px; padding-bottom: 21px; } @media screen and (min-width: 750px) { .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 28px; padding-bottom: 28px; } } FAQ What is the acoustic panel made of? The panel is made of a black acoustic felt (made of recycelt plastic). On top of that you find the slats with an MDF core and a veneer surface. How do I clean the acoustic panels? You best use a duster or a vacuum cleaner for the cleaning. Is the felt breathable? Yes, our acoustic felt is breathable. Are the surfaces treated? Can I oil them? The surfaces are in principle untreated.They can be oiled with a wood oil (not cooking oil) and a sponge or towel. What about the UV stability of the surfaces? The wood surfaces are untreated and will therefore change over time due to the effects of light. The light, classical oak, for example, turns typically a little yellowish. Do the panels also insulate the sound to the outside? Unfortunately, the panels won’t stop sound from wandering from room to room (or floor to floor) – their main purpose is to absorb reverberation and prevent it from being reflected back into the room. If you want to stop sound coming from a neighbour or a room, it needs good cavity insulation between walls or floors – and maybe more. On what surfaces can I install the panel? The installation is possible on nearly every surface, even on brick walls and concrete. Can I use the panels in the bathroom? In general, we do not recommend its use in damp rooms. The core consists of an MDF board, which could maybe swell. Nevertheless, some of our customers have used the acoustic panels in the bathroom and are very satisfied. However, it should be made sure that the product does not come into direct contact with water. How do I install electric lights and sockets? You can cut a hole into the panels and extract the socket end of the panel wall. Use electrician. How shall I mount the panels? If the panels are mainly used for visual purposes, it is possible to attach them directly to the wall. For this, we recommend the use of (black) screws, which are then drilled directly through the felt into the wall or also glued to the wall with mounting glue. To achieve sound class A, we recommend the mounting on 45mm thick battens. The resulting gap is then lined with mineral wool (we recommend Isover or Rockwool). Do you provide an installation service? We will come and install the panels , so you can sit back and relax. Can I place pictures on the panels? The picture frames can be stuck on with Tesa Foto Stripes, for example.Alternatively, a small nail/screw can be drilled through the felt into the wall. Can I hide cables behind the panels? This depends on the thickness of the cables. In general, the cables are simply positioned behind the panel, because the felt is very flexible and gives space at this point.

routes.text: .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 21px; padding-bottom: 21px; } @media screen and (min-width: 750px) { .section-template--25688773263739__main-padding { padding-top: 28px; padding-bottom: 28px; } } Fabric Care Guide Choose the Right Fabric — Keep It Looking Beautiful Curtains don’t just add style — the fabric you choose affects how your room feels, how much light it blocks, and how long it lasts. This guide helps you understand the most popular curtain fabrics and how to care for them properly. 🧵 Popular Curtain Fabrics 1. Cotton Look & Feel: Natural, breathable, and versatile. Best For: Living rooms, bedrooms. Care: Machine washable (check label), low-heat iron. 2. Linen / Linen Look Look & Feel: Light, airy, slightly textured. Best For: Light-filled rooms and relaxed settings. Care: Dry clean or gentle wash; may wrinkle. 3. Velvet Look & Feel: Luxurious, thick, and elegant. Best For: Bedrooms, formal lounges, thermal insulation. Care: Dry clean only; use a soft brush for dusting. 4. Polyester / Blends Look & Feel: Durable, crease-resistant, low-maintenance. Best For: Busy households, children's rooms. Care: Machine washable, easy iron. 5. Silk / Faux Silk Look & Feel: Smooth, elegant, and light-reflective. Whether you're using a curtain pole or track, we’ll help you get the perfect finish. 🛠️ What You’ll Need: Curtain pole or track Screws and wall plugs Drill and screwdriver Spirit level Pencil and measuring tape Step ladder Curtains (of course!) 🧭 Step 1: Mark the Position Use a tape measure and spirit level to mark where your pole or track brackets will go. We recommend placing your pole 15–20cm above the window and extending 15–30cm beyond each side for maximum coverage and light control. 🔩 Step 2: Fit the Brackets Drill holes where marked. Insert wall plugs (especially in plaster walls). Screw in the brackets firmly. Double-check the alignment with your level before tightening. 🪵 Step 3: Attach the Pole or Track For poles: Slide on curtain rings (if using) before attaching to brackets. Tab Top or Tie Top Curtains: Loop over the pole and tie or slide as needed. Make sure the curtains are evenly gathered and hang at the desired drop. ✅ Final Checks Adjust gathers or folds for a balanced look. Test draw the curtains to ensure smooth movement. Just follow our simple step-by-step guide to ensure a professional, made-to-measure finish. 🪟 Step 1: Decide Where You Want to Hang Your Curtains Option A: Above the Window Frame For a more dramatic look and to make the window appear taller, fit the pole or track 15–20cm (6–8 inches) above the window. Option B: Inside the Recess Ideal for a neat, flush look. Only use this option if you're not concerned about blocking out all light. 📏 Step 2: Measure the Width If Using a Curtain Pole: Measure the full width of the pole (excluding decorative finials). For gather fullness, multiply the pole width by: 1.5x for a standard gather 2x for a fuller, more luxurious look If Using a Curtain Track: Measure the full width of the track from end to end. 📐 Step 3: Measure the Drop (Height) Your drop measurement depends on how you want your curtains to fall: Heading Styles: Pencil Pleat / Eyelet / Tab Top: Measure from the top of the pole or track to where you want the curtain to end. Standard drop lengths: Sill, Below Sill, or Floor Length. Style Drop Point Sill length 1 cm above the windowsill Below sill 15–20 cm below the windowsill Floor length 1 cm above the floor (or longer for pooling) For eyelet curtains, measure from the top of the pole and add 2.5cm to account for the eyelet position. 🔧 Top Tip: Always use a metal tape measure for accuracy. Double-check each measurement twice. Make a note of any obstructions (radiators, handles, skirting) that may affect the curtain drop. Need Help? If you're unsure about measuring or need advice on tricky windows (like bay windows or apex shapes), our expert team is here to help. 📞 Call us: [0800 772 0367]📧 Email us: [enquiries@curtainsuk.com]

Whether you're looking to create a calm retreat, a vibrant statement, or a timeless backdrop, our colour guide will help you pick the perfect shade for your home. 1. Consider the Room's Purpose Living Room: Neutrals like beige, grey, and soft white create a welcoming atmosphere. For a bold look, try navy, forest green, or deep burgundy. For example, grey walls pair beautifully with mustard, teal, or blush curtains. 3. Natural Light & Fabric Weight In bright rooms, darker colours won’t overpower the space and can add depth. In low-light rooms, lighter colours help reflect light and make the space feel bigger. Heavier fabrics in darker colours are ideal for blocking light and adding warmth. 4. Trendy colours such as sage green, terracotta, and blush pink bring a modern flair—but consider how often you like to redecorate. 5. These derived records may be retained where required to operate and improve the service, including supporting your consultation, resuming your choices and reviewing service quality.
